reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of isotonic calibration is to transform a sequence of forecast probabilities into a monotonically increasing calibrated probability sequence, preserving order but adjusting for miscalibration. This is achieved using Pool Adjacent Violators Algorithm (PAVA), which pools adjacent elements violating monotonicity into weighted averages. The resulting step function ensures that higher forecasts correspond to higher calibrated probabilities. Brier decomposition separates total forecast error into three components: reliability (how close forecasts are to observed rates), resolution (ability to distinguish between classes), and uncertainty (base rate of outcomes). These components provide diagnostics for improving forecast quality. Reliability curves visualize this relationship by plotting mean forecast against observed frequency within bins. Together, these primitives form a coherent framework for evaluating and refining probabilistic forecasts, ensuring they meet the standard of being both calibrated and informative.
